tuner_timing.justification: To maximize throughput in this early exploration phase, we are aggressively tuning the scheduler for responsiveness and low latency by reducing granularity and wakeup times, while also preventing deep C-states and ensuring CPUs run at maximum performance. NAPI busy polling is introduced to potentially improve network throughput.

The previous iteration's throughput drop with POLL c-state suggests potential thermal or power management issues. This configuration explores a less aggressive C-state (C1) to balance power and performance, while introducing napi_busy_poll to improve network processing efficiency for throughput.

The best throughput was observed with 'unlimited' cstate_max and without napi_busy_poll. This configuration explores 'C6' as the deepest available C-state and disables napi_busy_poll to emulate the top-performing setup, while retaining the beneficial min_perf_pct setting.

To understand the interaction between latency_ns and napi_busy_poll, I am setting napi_busy_poll to 0 while keeping latency_ns at 30M and cstate_max at C6. This mimics the successful Iter 1 configuration's assumed napi_busy_poll value with Iter 7's latency_ns.

Based on previous iterations, napi_busy_poll=750 and cstate_max=C6 appear to be beneficial for throughput. This configuration explores slightly increased scheduler latencies (latency_ns, min_granularity_ns, wakeup_granularity_ns) to further reduce scheduling overhead and potentially maximize throughput.

Reverting to the best performing configuration (Iter 9) to re-evaluate its performance and confirm the sensitivity of latency_ns, especially after recent performance drops. This helps to rule out noise and pinpoint the optimal latency_ns value.

Given the significant jump in throughput (from 9.20 to 10.40) for the exact same configuration in previous iterations, re-running this configuration is crucial to confirm the stability and robustness of this promising region before further fine-tuning. This helps account for the observed workload noise.

The previous best configuration showed high variability due to noise. To further explore this promising region and potentially reduce scheduling overhead for higher throughput, we are slightly increasing the min and wakeup granularity while keeping other parameters stable.

Reverting min_granularity_ns and wakeup_granularity_ns to values that previously yielded the highest throughput (10.40) will help confirm if the previous increase was detrimental and if the optimal region is around the lower granularity settings. This is an exploitation step focusing on the region of the best observed performance.

The current best throughput was achieved with latency_ns=40,000,000. I am slightly decreasing latency_ns to 35,000,000 to explore a nearby value and check for a potential local optimum, while keeping other parameters stable.

We are refining the 'latency_ns' parameter around the previously observed peak of 40,000,000 ns, as this value consistently yielded high throughput. A slight increase will help confirm the optimal point in this region.

Continuing to refine the latency_ns parameter around the observed peak of 40M ns to confirm robustness and potentially find a slightly better optimum, given the noisy performance data. Other parameters remain at values that yielded high throughput.

Continuing to refine the latency_ns parameter around the observed peak of 40-42M, as previous trials in this range yielded the highest throughput. Other parameters are kept consistent with the best performing configurations.

Given the noisy data and the clustering of best performance around a latency_ns of 40-42M, I am making a small adjustment to latency_ns within this promising range to further explore the local optimum. Other parameters remain at their previously effective values.

The system has explored latency_ns with noisy results around the current best. To continue refining the optimal region for throughput, we will slightly increase min_granularity_ns and wakeup_granularity_ns to potentially further reduce scheduling overhead, while keeping other well-performing parameters constant.

Reverting to the best performing configuration from Iter 16 is crucial to re-validate its effectiveness and establish a stable baseline after a significant performance drop in the last iteration. This will help confirm the robustness of the optimal parameter set before further refinement.

We are refining parameters around the best observed configurations. We will slightly increase latency_ns to explore reducing context switching overhead further and maximize napi_busy_poll to potentially boost network throughput.

Reverting napi_busy_poll to 750 and setting latency_ns to 40,000,000 aims to re-evaluate the parameter combination that previously yielded the highest throughput. This strategy focuses on confirming the robustness of the best-performing region amidst noisy data.

We are in an exploitation phase, refining around the promising region. This slight adjustment to latency_ns aims to explore a finer granularity around the previously observed optimal values, considering the noisy nature of the performance metrics.

I am exploring the immediate vicinity of the optimal latency_ns values (40M and 42M) that yielded the best throughput, while keeping other parameters at their historically high-performing values. This helps confirm the robustness of the promising region amidst noisy measurements.
